comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
- Opt-in simple: it is the method of registration with a single click confirmation, once entered in the form the email address (among other information).

- Double opt-in or confirmed opt-in: includes an additional step to confirm the subscription. Once the form has been completed and the request has been sent, click on the confirmation message sent automatically to the new contact. A method to ensure that the email address entered is valid and that the user is the actual owner.

The Opt-in must register. Therefore, you should always be able to demonstrate how you have compiled the option so that its legal validity can be proven.

This issue GDPR Compliance #244 should be a priority, since all registered users (in beta for example) using forms that do not comply with the GDPR are illegal, and they would have to re-register once the form complies with the GDPR.

GDPR require that no cookie is accepted without consent (explicit consent, same that register form), not only a notice (implied), usually a warning is included in the cookie policy or in the same message indicating that some of them are technically necessary for the web to work. login etc.

### **full text of the article from the image above: Here is an explanation about the cookie consent :** https://www.cookiebot.com/en/cookie-consent/

It is the general norm, but I am not sure if it always applies to all cookies because sometimes there is a distinction between technical/necessary cookies and others, I think so, because get user personal data to remember preferences, etc (login= ¿user id, email, IP?).

I leave the link here in case someone needs to consult to make their compliance with GDPR in the future or it could be included in the forum although it is somewhat focused on jimdo.
https://jimdo-legal.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000189886-GDPR

P.S: I think you only have to worry about the cookies of the phpvms system.
Google adsense, G. analytics etc, it should be the work of the owner of the VA, but it would be good to leave a space in which putting the scripts of third parties, in a section of the code that you enable, be blocked or unlocked according to the user accept the cookies or not. It's what I wanted to say in my first message.
